label: scope
question: Какие прокси-признаки экспозиции (интенсивности движения, AADT) и пешеходной активности строят из открытых данных (OpenStreetMap: центральность графа betweenness/closeness, класс дороги, POI, остановки, здания; ночные снимки; население) для моделей аварийности ДТП на уровне ячеек/зон (macro-level crash prediction, area-level crash models, AADT estimation from OSM) — какие признаки реально работают, какой у них подтверждённый эффект, и какие кодировки (плотность на км, доли, лог) рекомендуются? Нужны конкретные статьи 2015–2026 с результатами.

angles.label: AADT estimation from OSM / open data (academic)
angles.query: AADT estimation OpenStreetMap road network betweenness centrality machine learning traffic volume prediction 2018..2026
angles.rationale: Core exposure proxy: papers that predict traffic volume from OSM topology/centrality and open data report feature importances and R2, directly showing which network features carry AADT signal.

angles.label: Macro-level / zonal crash models with exposure proxies
angles.query: macro-level crash frequency model traffic analysis zone exposure proxy population employment road density negative binomial ScienceDirect
angles.rationale: The classical zonal-safety literature (Lee, Abdel-Aty, Cai, Huang) establishes which area-level variables (VMT, road length by class, intersection density, population) are significant and how they are encoded (densities, logs).

angles.label: Pedestrian activity proxies and POI/transit features
angles.query: pedestrian exposure proxy POI density bus stops land use OpenStreetMap pedestrian crash model grid cells urban
angles.rationale: Pedestrian activity is the second exposure dimension: this surfaces work using POIs, transit stops, building footprints and Strava/mobile data as walking-volume proxies and their measured effect on pedestrian crashes.

angles.label: Nighttime lights / population rasters as exposure
angles.query: nighttime light VIIRS population density proxy road traffic crash risk spatial model grid WorldPop
angles.rationale: Remote-sensing proxies (VIIRS NTL, WorldPop/GHSL) are widely available for Russia and the question explicitly asks whether they add signal beyond OSM road features.

angles.label: Gridded ML crash-risk prediction with OSM features (practitioner/benchmarks)
angles.query: road accident risk prediction OpenStreetMap features grid cells gradient boosting feature importance hexagon H3 accident hotspot
angles.rationale: Applied ML papers and repos (H3 hex grids, XGBoost/CatBoost, DL on OSM tiles) show which engineered OSM features and encodings (per-km densities, shares, log) actually improve AUC in practice.

angles.label: Limitations and critiques of OSM-derived proxies
angles.query: limitations OpenStreetMap completeness bias proxy traffic volume crash model exposure measurement error centrality validation
angles.rationale: A skeptical angle: OSM completeness, centrality-vs-observed-flow validation studies and exposure measurement error warn which proxies are unreliable and how encoding choices bias estimates.

summary: Split the question along its three data layers (OSM network topology for AADT, POI/transit/buildings for pedestrian activity, NTL/population rasters) and its two literature streams (statistical zonal safety models vs. applied ML on grids), then add a contrarian angle on proxy validity and OSM completeness so the review of each feature's "common-sense adequacy" has evidence both for and against.
